blocks.title: Evaporation
blocks.text: Evaporation is the spontaneous conversion of a liquid into vapour at any temperature.

When high-energy molecules leave the liquid and low-energy molecules are left behind, the temperature of the liquid falls; heat then moves from the surroundings to the liquid, and the temperature of the surroundings falls too. This is why evaporation causes cooling. A person feels cool after a bath when water evaporates from the body in the air: the water molecules take away the body's energy. Earthenware vessels keep water cool in the same way: they are porous, water molecules with enough kinetic energy to overcome the intermolecular forces come out through the pores and evaporate, the energy for this comes from the liquid, so the average kinetic energy of the remaining water molecules falls and the water cools.
